extraction_sources: Dressing the Man - Alan Flusser - Chapter 3: Proportion
Dressing the Man - Alan Flusser - Chapter 4: The Prerogatives of Pattern
Gentleman's Gazette - How Patterns Can Sculpt Your Body Type
Put This On - How a Suit Jacket Should Fit

parameters.name: line_direction
parameters.description: The directional emphasis created by clothing lines (seams, stripes, lapels, creases). The most fundamental visual balance tool.

values.definition: North-south lines elongate and narrow the figure. Created by: pinstripes, front creases, long lapels, single-breasted openings, suspenders, monochrome dressing.
East-west lines broaden and shorten the figure. Created by: belts, cuffs, contrast between top/bottom halves, pocket flaps, wide checks. On 3D bodies, horizontal stripes make a person look wider.

Slanting lines slim the figure and lead the eye away from the center of the torso. Created by: double-breasted lapels, hacking pockets, angled pocket squares. The DB's diagonal lapels 'lead the eye away from the center of the torso.'

parameters.name: pattern_type
parameters.description: Classification of fabric patterns by their visual structure

values.definition: No pattern. Neutral visual effect. Monochrome dressing with solids creates maximum vertical elongation.
Linear repeating pattern. Subtypes: pinstripe (~1/30 inch), pencil (~1/8 inch), chalk (variable width), awning (~1/4 inch). Direction determines elongating vs broadening effect.
Grid-based pattern. Subtypes: micro-check, gingham, windowpane, Prince of Wales, tartan, houndstooth. Shape (square vs rectangular) determines directional emphasis.
Very small repeated imagery. Includes miniature versions of checks, stripes, paisleys, Macclesfield. Small patterns make the body appear larger in comparison.
Overlapping horizontal and vertical stripes forming a grid. Horizontal formation of checks, overplaids, and box-like designs beneficial for breaking vertical dominance in tall men.

parameters.name: pattern_scale
parameters.description: Size of the pattern relative to the wearer's body. Key principle: pattern scale should harmonize with body type.

values.definition: Very small patterns. Makes the body appear larger in comparison. Good for thin/slim men. Avoid on tall men (creates 'skyscraper' effect).
Fine patterns like pinstripes, small checks. Narrow-to-medium-spaced stripes for thin physique.
Moderate scale. Works for most body types. Standard pencil stripes, medium checks.

Bold patterns, wide stripes, large checks, overplaids. Tall men can wear larger-scaled patterns. Slightly broader, less pronounced lines for fuller figures. Larger prints minimize perception of width for wide men.

parameters.name: pattern_spacing
parameters.description: Distance between repeating elements in a pattern

values.definition: Tightly spaced patterns. Close-together stripes help appear taller. Multi-color close stripes enhance height.
Widely spaced patterns. Better for thin individuals to appear broader.

parameters.name: pattern_orientation
parameters.description: The directional emphasis of a check or rectangular pattern

values.definition: Rectangular checks that are taller than wide emphasize length and height. Good for short men.
Square checks have neutral directional effect.
Rectangular checks wider than tall emphasize width. Good for tall/thin men who want to appear broader.

parameters.name: color_value_contrast
parameters.description: The lightness/darkness of colors and contrast between garment zones

values.definition: Dark colors recede, minimize, and slim. Medium-to-dark register recommended for stout physiques. Dark from top to bottom creates maximum elongation.
Moderate color values. Versatile, neither expanding nor minimizing.
Light colors advance, expand, and make areas appear larger. Thin men can use lighter colors to add visual volume. 'Light and bright color tops to emphasize chest area.'
Bright and vibrant colors make you 'stick out against your background' and appear bigger. Avoid for wide men; good for thin men who want presence.
Muted colors minimize size emphasis. Recommended for wide/heavy men.

parameters.name: top_bottom_contrast
parameters.description: Degree of color/pattern contrast between upper and lower body halves. Critical for perceived height.

values.definition: One color from top to bottom. Creates unbroken vertical line. Maximum elongation. Flusser: 'the suit's ultimate color lesson' for short/heavy men. The coordinating benchmark for this body type.
Similar but not identical tones top and bottom. Still elongates. Recommended for height-challenged men.
Pronounced difference between upper and lower halves. Divides the figure in half, shortening apparent height. Short men should avoid. Tall men can use to break vertical dominance.

parameters.name: silhouette_type
parameters.description: The overall outline/shape created by clothing on the body. Put This On: 'Style is about silhouette, whereas fit is about whether something sits on you correctly.'

values.definition: Built-up shoulders, defined waist, sharp lines. British tailoring tradition. Adds formality and authority.
Minimal padding, follows body's natural lines. American/Brooks Brothers tradition. Understated, relaxed authority.
Unstructured or lightly structured, fluid fabric. Italian tradition (Armani era). More relaxed, modern feel.
Close to the body, minimal excess fabric. Modern cut. Can accentuate narrow frame negatively if too tight.
Generous cut with room. Straight-hanging lines. Recommended for heavy men — close-fitting clothes reveal more than they conceal.

parameters.name: fit_quality
parameters.description: How well a garment sits on the body. Distinct from silhouette — fit rules are consistent across all styles.

values.definition: No pulls, puckers, X-shaped tension lines, or gaps. Collar glued to neck. Sleeves hang smooth. Vents closed. Clean lines all around.
X-shaped lines at waist button. Collar pulls. Vents flare open. Horizontal stress lines. 'Nothing like the look of a stuffed sausage.'
Excess fabric, pooling, sleeves flapping at wrist. Creates visual bulk and heft. Jacket appears to hang off the body.

parameters.name: visual_weight_distribution
parameters.description: Where visual mass/emphasis is concentrated on the body. Determined by garment structure, fabric, color, and detailing.

values.definition: Visual emphasis on upper body — broad shoulders, wide lapels, light-colored tops. Athletic/inverted triangle default. Goal: redirect weight downward.
Even distribution of visual weight. The ideal. Achieved through proportional detailing across all zones.
Visual emphasis on lower body — wider hips, heavy shoes, dark tops with light bottoms. Triangle body default. Goal: redirect weight upward.

parameters.name: pattern_mixing_count
parameters.description: How many distinct patterns are combined in one ensemble (suit + shirt + tie). Flusser Ch 4 dedicates the entire chapter to pattern mixing as a core proportion skill.

values.definition: One pattern + solids. Safest. No coordination skill required.
Two patterned garments + one solid. First level of pattern mixing. Rules depend on whether patterns are same or different design.
Three patterned garments. Requires consistent level of contrast and scale. Each design should differ from the others for safest result. 'Reward and risk go hand in hand.'
Expert level. Scale and degree of contrast must be mutual across all components. 'The more imagination and taste one puts into his appearance, the more subtle the results should be.'

parameters.name: pattern_mixing_relationship
parameters.description: Whether combined patterns share the same design type or are different. This determines which scale rule applies — the rules are OPPOSITE for same vs different designs.

values.definition: Two stripes together, or two checks together. Scale must be AS DIFFERENT AS POSSIBLE — otherwise similarity produces optical vibration/movement. Example: wide-spaced repp tie with close-set striped shirt.
Stripe + check, or plaid + stripe. Scale should be KEPT CLOSE IN SIZE. A dominant-patterned shirt requires a necktie with a design at least equal in scale.

parameters.name: pattern_scale_graduation
parameters.description: When mixing 3+ patterns, the principle of graduating scale from smallest at base (shirt) to largest outward (jacket/tie).

values.definition: Start with smallest pattern at base (shirt), build up to jacket's larger pattern, extend outward to pocket square. Infuses arrangement with dimension and proportion.
When two of three patterns share a design (e.g., two checks + one stripe), the odd one out must take its cue from the more prominent of the two partners.

parameters.name: pattern_color_connection
parameters.description: Patterns harmonize better when they share at least one color. Flusser repeatedly shows how a tie's color reflecting the suit's overcheck or the shirt's tone advances the combination.

values.definition: At least one color in common between patterned garments. The tie's color reflecting that of the shirt or suit further advances the combination's harmony.
No color linkage between patterns. Higher risk of discord. Requires exceptional scale management to compensate.

parameters.name: detail_density
parameters.description: Amount of visual details/interruptions in the outfit. Details (pocket flaps, ticket pockets, turn-back cuffs) break vertical sweeps.

values.definition: Few details. Clean vertical lines. Promotes elongation. Better for short/heavy men — 'less is more' (Flusser). Jetted pockets, no change pocket, no sleeve cuffs.
Standard detailing. Flap pockets, visible cuffs. Balanced visual effect.
Multiple details — ticket pockets, patch pockets, flaps, turn-back sleeve cuffs. 'Stylish clutter' that impedes long vertical sweeps. Beneficial for tall men to break height dominance.

parameters.name: fabric_surface
parameters.description: Visual and tactile quality of fabric surface. Affects perceived bulk and formality.

values.definition: Fine worsteds, poplin. Minimizes thickness and bulk. Better for heavy men. More formal.
Flannels, cheviots, tweeds, surface-interest woolens. Adds visual weight and bulk. Better for thin men. More casual.

parameters.name: style_priority_hierarchy
parameters.description: The order of importance when building an outfit. From Real Men Real Style's Style Pyramid concept.

values.definition: Most important. A well-fitting inexpensive suit beats a poorly-fitting expensive one. 'Proper fitting can do much for an inexpensive suit, while a poor fit can scuttle the expensively hand-tailored creation' (Flusser).
Second priority. Material quality determines drape, texture, and longevity. Affects how the silhouette reads.
Third priority. Appropriateness for the occasion and context. A perfectly fitted suit is wrong at a beach party.

theoretical_frameworks.name: helmholtz_illusion
theoretical_frameworks.description: On 2D flat surfaces, horizontal stripes make a shape appear ~6% thinner. On 3D bodies, the effect REVERSES — horizontal stripes make a person look wider. This is critical: fashion advice based on 2D illusion research is misleading.

theoretical_frameworks.name: inverse_scale_principle
theoretical_frameworks.description: Pattern size inversely affects perceived body size. Smaller patterns make the body appear larger in comparison. Larger patterns make the body appear smaller in comparison. This is the foundation of pattern-to-body-type matching.

theoretical_frameworks.name: flusser_fulcrum_principle
theoretical_frameworks.description: The waist button is to a suit jacket what a fulcrum is to a seesaw. Raise it too much = torso abbreviated. Lower it too much = torso elongated at expense of leg line. Correct position: 1/2 inch below natural waist. Divides body so torso and legs appear at maximum length.

theoretical_frameworks.name: flusser_frame_principle
theoretical_frameworks.description: Every element frames the adjacent element: collar frames the face, jacket frames the shirt, trouser frames the shoe. A small picture requires a like-scaled frame. Each frame must be proportional to what it contains.

theoretical_frameworks.name: jacket_length_rule
theoretical_frameworks.description: Two methods: (1) Arm dropped at side — jacket bottom lines up with outstretched thumb. (2) Distance from collar seam to floor, divided in half. Must cover curvature of buttocks while giving leg as long a line as possible.

theoretical_frameworks.name: lapel_width_rule
theoretical_frameworks.description: Single-breasted lapel should cover 2/5 to 3/5 of the distance between jacket's chest and shoulder line. Results in notch lapel measuring 3 3/8 to 4 1/4 inches. Broader shoulders = broader lapels for balance.

theoretical_frameworks.name: tie_width_rule
theoretical_frameworks.description: Necktie width determined by jacket lapel width. Narrow shoulders = less chest = narrower lapel = narrower tie. Equivalent range of bottom widths (3 3/8 to 4 1/4 inches) immunizes neckties from fashion vagaries.

theoretical_frameworks.name: trouser_shoe_harmony
theoretical_frameworks.description: Trouser bottom should cover about two-thirds of the shoe. Width must harmonize with shoe scale. Narrow bottoms + large feet = feet loom larger. Wide bottoms + small feet = feet appear smaller.

theoretical_frameworks.name: style_vs_fit_distinction
theoretical_frameworks.description: Style is about silhouette (the overall outline). Fit is about whether something sits on you correctly. Silhouettes vary by era and taste. Fit rules remain constant. A well-fitting garment has no pulls, puckers, X-tension, gaps, or ripples.

theoretical_frameworks.name: alterability_hierarchy
theoretical_frameworks.description: Some fit issues are easily fixed, others are difficult/costly. Easy: waist suppression, back smoothness. Difficult: shoulders, collar balance, sleeve pitch, vents. Critical fit points should work right off the rack — buy for shoulders, alter for waist.

theoretical_frameworks.name: flusser_pattern_mixing_scale_rules
theoretical_frameworks.description: Flusser Ch 4 central principle: scale is the primary tool for harmonizing patterns. Two OPPOSITE rules apply depending on whether patterns share the same design or not. (1) Same design (two stripes, two checks): vary scale AS MUCH AS POSSIBLE — similarity produces optical vibration. (2) Different designs (stripe + check): keep scale CLOSE — this harmonizes unlike patterns. When mixing 3+, graduate from small (shirt) to large (outward). The more patterns combined, the more subtle the overall effect must be.

theoretical_frameworks.name: flusser_small_pattern_danger
theoretical_frameworks.description: Two small patterns placed near each other, whether similar or not, wreak havoc on the viewer's eye. One design must be significantly larger. You rarely see two small patterns on television because their vibrating effect distorts the camera's focus.
